label: Micius to Xinglong (Liao 2017) with turbulence coupling, 10 urad field stop
source: Liao et al., Nature 549, 43 (2017), arXiv:1707.00542; seeing from Zhang et al., arXiv:1601.08114 (2016); turbulence relations from Liu et al., arXiv:1505.05436
note: The default Micius link plus the optional turbulence coupling loss (Round 78, the user's choice): the seeing-limited image grows as the satellite sinks and a small field stop loses its edge. Xinglong's field stop is not published, so its size here is an assumption; at 10 urad it steepens the 19 December 2016 pass from 8.4 to 9.6 dB against Liao's 10.8.

orbit_altitude_km.quote: successfully launched on 16th August 2016, from Jiuquan, China, orbiting at an altitude of ~500 km

station_altitude_km.quote: Xinglong ground observatory station (near Beijing, 40 deg 23' 45.12'' N, 117 deg 34' 38.85'' E, altitude 890m)

beam_divergence_urad.quote: sends the light beam with a near-diffraction-limited far-field divergence of ~10 urad

rx_aperture_m.quote: a Ritchey-Chretien telescope with an aperture of 1 m and a focal length of 10 m (Fig. 1c) is used to receive the QKD photons

receiver_optics_efficiency.quote: The overall optical efficiency including the receiving telescope and the fiber coupling on the ground station is ~16%

atmospheric_db.quote: We estimate that at 1200 km the loss due to atmospheric absorption and turbulence is in the range of 3 dB to 8 dB
atmospheric_db.note: The midpoint, scaled to other ranges by air mass (Round 77, the user's choice). Over the 19 December 2016 pass it gives 1 percent fewer detections than Liao counted (3,517,343 against 3,551,136).

atmospheric_ref_km.quote: at 1200 km the loss due to atmospheric absorption and turbulence is in the range of 3 dB to 8 dB

pointing_db.quote: the loss due to pointing error is less than 3 dB
pointing_db.note: The upper value; not scaled with elevation.

detector_efficiency.quote: four single-photon detectors (efficiency 50%, dark counts <25 Hz, timing jitter 350 ps)

dark_count_prob.quote: dark counts <25 Hz ... tag the received signal photons within a 2-ns time window
dark_count_prob.note: 25 per second times 2e-9 s, per detector per pulse.

misalignment.quote: the observed quantum bit error rate (QBER) with an average of 1.1%, consistent with the expected error rate due to background noise and polarization visibility
misalignment.note: Used as the error floor: this model has no separate background-light term.

source_rate_hz.quote: Eight fiber-based laser diodes ... emit laser pulses (848.6 nm, 100 MHz, 0.2 ns)

detector_dead_time_s.assumption: Liao et al. state no dead time. At the downlink's ~1e4 detections per second a dead time under a microsecond costs under 1 percent, so none is modelled rather than one invented.

mu_signal.quote: the average photon number in the output of the telescope: mu_s=0.8, mu_1=0.1, mu_2=0

mu_decoy.quote: the average photon number in the output of the telescope: mu_s=0.8, mu_1=0.1, mu_2=0

p_signal.quote: a high mu_s, a moderate mu_1 and a zero mu_2 (vacuum), sent with probabilities of 50%, 25%, and 25%, respectively

p_decoy.quote: a high mu_s, a moderate mu_1 and a zero mu_2 (vacuum), sent with probabilities of 50%, 25%, and 25%, respectively

vacuum_decoy.quote: Here we adopt a 3-intensity protocol using three levels of mu: a high mu_s, a moderate mu_1 and a zero mu_2 (vacuum)
vacuum_decoy.note: So the vacuum yield is measured and the bound is Ma et al. 2005's Vacuum+Weak estimate (Eq. 34 and Eq. 37), not the one-decoy Eq. (41).

min_elevation_deg.quote: A single-orbit experiment ends when the satellite reaches 10 deg elevation angle in the other end
min_elevation_deg.note: Liao's passes start 'From about 15 deg elevation angle'; one threshold serves both ends here. Sidhu et al., arXiv:2602.11833 (2026), also impose 10 degrees.

distance_km.assumption: The page's default slant range, inside the 645-1200 km of the 19 December 2016 pass.

field_stop_urad.assumption: Xinglong's field stop is not published - Liao et al. 2018 say only that the decoders are 'designed with a small field-of-view'. 10 urad is the radius at which this term begins to matter; Zvenigorod's receiver accepts 25 urad (Khmelev et al. 2023), where it adds almost nothing.

seeing_arcsec.quote: Mean and median seeing are around 1.9'' and 1.7'', respectively (Zhang et al., arXiv:1601.08114: Xinglong's DIMM, 2014)
seeing_arcsec.note: Taken as the seeing at 500 nm and the zenith, DIMM's usual convention; the paper does not restate it.

wavelength_nm.quote: emit laser pulses (848.6 nm, 100 MHz, 0.2 ns)
